name: mellin_cpow_smul
result.signature: (f : ℝ → E) (s a : ℂ) : mellin (fun t => (t : ℂ) ^ a • f t) s = mellin f (s + a)
result.type:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℂ E] (f : ℝ → E) (s a : ℂ),
  mellin (fun t => ↑t ^ a • f t) s = mellin f (s + a)
result.value:
:= by
  refine setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Ioi fun t ht => ?_
  simp_rw [← sub_add_eq_add_sub, cpow_add _ _ (ofReal_ne_zero.2 <| ne_of_gt ht), mul_smul]
result.informal_description: For any function $ f : \mathbb{R} \to E $ and complex numbers $ s, a \in \mathbb{C} $, the Mellin transform of the function $ t \mapsto t^a \cdot f(t) $ evaluated at $ s $ equals the Mellin transform of $ f $ evaluated at $ s + a $. Symbolically, $ \mathcal{M}\{t^a \cdot f(t)\}(s) = \mathcal{M}\{f\}(s + a) $.

result.informal_name: Mellin Transform Convergence under Multiplication by $ t^a $ and Parameter Shift
result.informal_description: For a function $ f : \mathbb{R} \to E $ and complex parameters $ s, a $, the Mellin transform of $ t^a \cdot f(t) $ converges at $ s $ if and only if the Mellin transform of $ f $ converges at $ s + a $. This equivalence relates the convergence of the transformed function $ t \mapsto t^a \cdot f(t) $ to a shifted parameter domain of the original function.

name: mellin
result.type: {E : Type u_1} → [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] → [NormedSpace ℂ E] → (ℝ → E) → ℂ → E
result.value:
:=
  ∫ t : ℝ in Ioi 0, (t : ℂ) ^ (s - 1) • f t
result.informal_description: The Mellin transform of a function $ f : \mathbb{R} \to E $ at a complex number $ s $ is defined as the Bochner integral over $ (0, \infty) $ of $ t^{s - 1} \cdot f(t) $ with respect to the Lebesgue measure, resulting in an element of the Banach space $ E $.

name: mellin_div_const
result.signature: (f : ℝ → ℂ) (s a : ℂ) : mellin (fun t => f t / a) s = mellin f s / a
result.type: ∀ (f : ℝ → ℂ) (s a : ℂ), mellin (fun t => f t / a) s = mellin f s / a
result.informal_description: For any function $ f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C} $ and complex numbers $ s $ and $ a $, the Mellin transform of the function $ t \mapsto \frac{f(t)}{a} $ evaluated at $ s $ is equal to the Mellin transform of $ f $ at $ s $ divided by $ a $. Mathematically, $ \mathcal{M}(f/a)(s) = \mathcal{M}f(s)/a $, where $ \mathcal{M} $ denotes the Mellin transform.
